etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English, from Old French contingent (whence con- and -ent), from Medieval Latin contingens (“possible, contingent”), present participle of contingere (“to touch, meet, attain to, happen”), from com- (“together”) + tangere (“to touch”).
senses: An event which may or may not happen; that which is unforeseen, undetermined, or dependent on something in the future.
That which falls to one in a division or apportionment among a number; a suitable share.
Possible or liable, but not certain, to occur.
